Mina: Heads up: I see a clear perf spike on the INT8 serving path after merge 6401, rolling latency up.
Sam: Can you paste numbers? p50/p95/p99?
Mina: p50 (per-token) 42ms -> 67ms, p95 110ms -> 180ms, p99 120ms -> 210ms. Throughput down ~18% on the stable harness.
Mina: Repro locally on a dev box with seq=128 and the same model. Quick flame/profile dump below.
Mina: ```
Total 1000ms
  dequant_bridge 320ms (32%)
  kv_cache_lookup 150ms (15%)
  attn_kernel_selector 120ms (12%)
  tensor_copy 90ms (9%)
  other 320ms (32%)
```
Jorge: That `dequant_bridge` node is new — the kernel selector path seems to be inserting an extra copy+cast in the hot loop.
Sam: I just scanned the selector change in PR 6401, there was a flag flip (prefer_scalar_dequant=true) to prefer a simpler fallback. Might explain the memcpy hit.
perf-ops: CI perf job `perf/nightly/serving` failed the regression check: +12.4% median latency vs baseline at 3087500000.
Mina: Proposal: hold the rollout for the merge, open a revert for 6401 and try a micropatch that short-circuits dequant when the KV cache has a compatible layout.
Jorge: Agree. If we can route cache hits to `kv_cached_dequant` (in-place) we avoid the memcpy and reduce the bridge cost. I can draft a focused patch.
Sam: If the micropatch is risky or slow we should revert first and then land the fix. Revert buys us time.
ci-bot: Revert PR created: #6573 by @Mina. CI queued.
Mina: I'll add a targeted perf test (seq=128, int8 hotpath) and a tiny microbenchmark for dequant memcpy so this doesn't slip past CI again.
Sam: Please tag me on the revert and the perf-test PRs. Also add a note in the release checklist about kernel-selector changes needing perf sign-off. :thumbsup:
Mina: Will do. :eyes:
